source.title: PreciseCoder: Faithful and Generalizable Debugging Beyond Unit-Test Rewards
source.authors: Yun-Kai Zhan; Miao-Sen Chai; Shang-Shang Wang; Ji-Ke Zhong; Yuqing Yang; Deqing Fu; Serina Chang; Wang Bill Zhu

page_placements.theme: A weaker model's text inserted into a stronger model's inference (rewritten prompts, RL-trained instructions, critiques, short reasoning segments)

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses weak-to-strong generalization as background but tests transfer of an editing discipline through reasoning traces, not fine-tuning a strong model on weaker-model labels or the claim's PGR.
record.gate_note: The paper reports reasoning-trace transfer results for editing precision and pass rate. These concern a related but different transfer mechanism and measure, so they are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as results for V1–V6. The other debugging and reward results do not test weak-to-strong training on weak labels.
record.test_reason: This study does not fine-tune a strong model on a weaker model's labels and computes no PGR. Its 'weak-to-strong transfer' (§5.2) is a different mechanism. A trained 9B model's reasoning trace is prefilled into a receiver's thinking, or pasted into the user turn, with no weight updates. The receivers mostly already beat the donor on pass rate. The study cites Burns et al. only as background for the framing. The trace-transfer results therefore belong under fits_no_version, not V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the PreciseCoder-9B think block raises edit precision of stronger receivers by 4.6–12.4 points at roughly their own pass rates, with no weights, tokenizer or training shared. Prefilled into its own base, the trace recovers 73% of the pass gain and 60% of the precision gain. They attribute the transfer to naming buggy lines and weighing each edit. They frame it as an editing discipline, not a capability, passed from a small model.
record.recipe_differences: Reasoning-trace prompting/prefill transfer rather than fine-tuning a strong student on labels produced by a weaker supervisor; the study does not calculate PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Trace-transfer outcomes vary with receiver and donor trace; the paper also distinguishes prefilled traces with continued reasoning from traces supplied in the user turn.

fits_no_version.finding: A PreciseCoder-9B think block, prefilled or pasted, raises edit precision of five stronger receivers by 4.6–12.4 points. Their pass rates move −1.5 to +4.3 points. An untrained 9B trace costs the 27B receiver 7.4 pass points. The 27B receiver's precision gain grows with how precision-trained the donor is (+2.6 base, +7.4 GRPO, +10.1 PreciseCoder mean, +11.1 EA-GRPO).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A smaller trained model's reasoning trace can transfer an editing discipline (precision) to stronger models at inference, without weight updates. Gains depend on the donor's training.

record.problems: The reported transfer is a different intervention from weak-label fine-tuning and does not measure PGR. Table 4 does not give numeric own-reasoning baselines for several receivers, although it reports changes from those baselines. Transfer findings are task-specific to PDB Test.
record.rows_left_out: No other study results were included because the remaining reported debugging, hallucination, reward-ablation, and benchmark outcomes do not test weak-to-strong fine-tuning on weaker-model labels.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning a strong student on weak labels; beating the weak supervisor; PGR.
Training changes to weak-to-strong fine-tuning and their effect on PGR.
PGR dependence on supervisor and student size, task, or representations.
Exploiting the weak supervisor's blind spots, distribution shift, shared errors.
Theory of when a student must beat its supervisor.

record.verdict_notes: Weak-to-strong appears only as a framing label for inference-time trace transfer. Note the likely value error in R2: own-base prefilled precision is 58.4%, not 64.6%. Duplicate rows R3/R13, R4/R14 and R19/R20 should be merged. Numeric baselines for Table 4 receivers can be read from Table 2 or derived from the Δs.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning a strong model on labels produced by a weaker supervisor, beating that supervisor, and PGR.
Training changes to weak-to-strong fine-tuning and their effect on PGR.
PGR variation by supervisor/student size, task, or representations.
Weak-supervisor blind spots, distribution shift in weak-to-strong training, and shared-error effects.
Theoretical conditions for a student to beat its supervisor.
Weak-to-strong effects in vision or other non-language modalities.
